# Refusal Parity: is safety repair language-fair?

[![CI](https://github.com/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Code: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/code-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Data: CC BY-NC 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/data-CC%20BY--NC%204.0-lightgrey.svg)](LICENSE-DATA)
[![Python 3.12](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12-blue.svg)](pyproject.toml)
[![Data on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20data-refusal--parity-yellow.svg)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity)

**Abdullah Ibn Mahdi Abtahi** · Ingramin ·
paper: [`paper/main.pdf`](paper/main.pdf) · v0.2.0

This repository audits whether *refusal repair* (activation steering gated per prompt, and weight-space repair) treats
languages fairly. The study model is Cohere's Tiny Aya (3.35B). It covers ten [MultiJail](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DAMO-NLP-SG/MultiJail)
languages in three resource tiers and has a pre-registered analysis plan. The pipeline is built on the Lexsi
open-source stack: **CuratorKIT → CircuitKIT → SafeTune → AuditKIT**.

> ⚠️ **Content warning.** The evaluation uses harmful requests from public red-teaming benchmarks, and some model
> responses are harmful. Responses and steering artifacts are distributed only through gated Hugging Face repos.

## Main findings (Tiny Aya Earth, A100, Qwen3Guard-4B; v0.2.0)

Values are generated from the result files by the same macros as the paper: the threshold-rule rows from `runs/controls_report.json` and `runs/arms_report.json` (read by the dated pre-registration rules), the detector row from `runs/B0/h1.json`, the comparator row from `runs/GEM-lite/judged.jsonl`. 95% paired bootstrap intervals over prompt ids.

| Finding | Estimate |
|---|---|
| At a matched false-refusal budget (ε = .05), per-language split-conformal thresholds vs one pooled threshold: worst-language benign refusal | **34.9% → 25.5%**, -9.4 pp [-15.1, -3.8]; mean -1.0 pp [-2.2, +0.0] |
| …and the price: harmful-prompt refusal in the low-resource tier (Bengali, Swahili, Javanese) | -7.5 pp [-9.6, -5.4]; Javanese -14.4, Italian +6.2 |
| Per-language false-firing bound on held-out prompts: languages above the predictive band | 0 of 10 at ε = .05, 0 of 10 at ε = .10 |
| Gate separates XSTest's unsafe from safe contrast prompts (harm, not only dataset style) | AUROC 0.81 (every language ≥ 0.78) |
| A benign "Good morning." prefix (ε = .10), mean benign refusal of the repaired model | 20% → 64% (`EORS-S`), 21% → 64% (`CPOOL-S`); unrepaired 11% → 13% |
| SafeTune's English keyword refusal detectors: highest recall outside English | 0% |
| Closed comparator (Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite) safe-response rate: same-family judge vs Qwen3Guard (post hoc) | 99.3% vs 93.6% |

Equal false-refusal rates across languages whose gate-score distributions differ force unequal protection. Which error to equalise is a deployment decision; the paper reports both at matched budgets.

## How the study is organised

| Stage | What happens | Code | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Data | MultiJail (harmful) + XSTest-safe translated with NLLB (benign), QA by GlotLID and back-translation chrF; CuratorKIT clean / dedup / provenance; ids kept only if parallel in all 10 languages | `translate_xstest.py`, `build_data.py` | `data/eval.jsonl` |
| 2. Activations | Last-token residual stream at every layer (decoder only, hooks) | `mech.py`, `gate_acts.py` | `runs/mech_*`, `runs/gate_acts_*` |
| 3. Arms | Steering vectors, condition directions and gate thresholds fitted offline from calibration activations; built on SafeTune's `CASTModel` | `arms.py`, `steer.py` | `arm_config.json` per run |
| 4. Generation | AuditKIT `generate` with each arm (A100 via `scripts/colab_gen.sh`) | `run_arm.py`, `generate.py` | `runs/<arm>/responses.jsonl` |
| 5. Scoring | AuditKIT `evaluate`: Qwen3Guard-4B (primary), SafeTune keyword detectors, GlotLID fidelity, Gemini (secondary) | `audit.py`, `judge.py`, `gemini.py` | `runs/<arm>/judged.jsonl` |
| 6. Analysis | Paired McNemar (Holm) and paired bootstrap over prompt ids; pre-registered contrasts only | `analyze.py`, `arms_report.py`, `controls_report.py` | `runs/arms_report.json`, `runs/controls_report.json` |
| 7. Paper | Every number is a generated LaTeX macro with its source; figures carry provenance JSON | `paper_numbers.py`, `figures_core.py` | `paper/` |

Supporting modules:
- `common.py`: paths, languages, constrained GlotLID;
- `lazy_sd.py`: streamed safetensors for ReSta;
- `cohere_style.py`: figure style.

Supporting scripts, each with a docstring stating its purpose, the paper section it serves and its outputs:
- judge validation: `build_pgp_val.py`, `validate_judges.py`;
- steering strength: `alpha_pick.py`;
- hypotheses: `h1.py`, `h3.py`;
- gate diagnostics: `gate_proxy.py`, `failure_gate.py`, `spoof.py`;
- CircuitKIT: `colab_circuit.py`, `circuit_spec.py`, `circuits.py`;
- logging and environment: `track.py` (MLflow), `smoke_test.py` (environment check).

## Reproduce

```bash
make setup          # Python 3.12 venv with the exact versions in pyproject.toml (uv)
make data           # released data from Hugging Face -> data/, runs/ (GATED=1 adds responses and activations)
make test           # unit tests, CPU, under a minute
make report         # pre-registered comparisons (the gate-level part needs GATED=1)
make verify         # rerun the analysis; fails unless every paper number is reproduced byte for byte (GATED=1)
make numbers paper  # regenerate every number and the PDF (GATED=1)
```

Requirements: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and [tectonic](https://tectonic-typesetting.github.io/) for the PDF.

GPU stages (activations, generation, scoring) ran on a Colab A100, driven by `scripts/colab_gen.sh`. It needs
`COLAB_SSH_KEY` and an HF token with access to the gated Tiny Aya repos; its header documents the arguments and the
token handling. Comparisons never mix hardware: every steering arm is paired with an unrepaired reference generated
on the same A100 (`E0_a100`).

## Released data

| Repository | Access | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| [`refusal-parity`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity) | open | Prompts, per-response labels (no response text), every summary file, paper and figures |
| [`refusal-parity-responses`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity-responses) | gated | Model responses (some harmful), judge-validation items |
| [`refusal-parity-steering`](https://huggingface.co/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity-steering) | gated | Steering vectors, condition directions, thresholds, activations |

## Repository layout

```
src/        pipeline and analysis (one module per stage; see the table above)
scripts/    remote-GPU drivers, release build, data fetch, reproduction check
tests/      unit tests: statistics, gate routing, label loading, data invariants
paper/      LaTeX sources, generated numbers and tables, figures with provenance JSON, PDF
research/   pre-registration and deviations log, premortems, research diary
release/    Hugging Face card templates (filled from the paper's numbers) and licence texts
```

**Determinism.**
- Seeds are fixed: data splits and the per-language paired bootstrap 20261026; tier and difference-in-differences bootstraps 20261027; calibration fold split 20261028.
- Decoding is greedy.
- A100 and Apple-MPS generations differ slightly, so results are reported per hardware (`runs/E0_a100/hardware_check.json`).

## Pre-registration and research record

- [`research/00_research_plan.md`](research/00_research_plan.md): the analysis plan and its dated deviations log. Every
  design change is logged before the result it concerns.
- [`research/11_controls_premortem.md`](research/11_controls_premortem.md): the controls added after independent review.
- [`research/DIARY.md`](research/DIARY.md): decisions, failures and lessons, in order.
